title: Research real-estate inquiry and tour handoffs; recommend buyer-interest routing
description:
Goal: Improve how the 323 Colonial house website processes purchase interest and directs prospective buyers to the right realtor, broker, or showing channel. Research only; leave ongoing work in other sessions untouched.

Scope:
- Examine Realtor.com, Redfin, Zillow, and at least two other major real-estate listing or brokerage sites. Choose additional sites for relevant, distinct handoff patterns.
- Trace listing-page calls to action: contact agent/broker, call/email, request information, request a tour/showing, and scheduling. Distinguish listing agent/broker from buyer-agent introductions, paid lead routing, or platform concierge where evidence supports it.
- Record destination, recipient clarity, required fields, sign-in gates, consent/disclosures, scheduling request versus confirmed appointment, visible confirmation/next steps, and mobile behavior. Clearly label anything inaccessible or not verifiable without a real submission.
- Inspect this project's existing buyer-interest flow at execution time: entry points, destinations, recipient ownership, and gaps. Do not assume concurrent work has left it unchanged.
- Recommend the smallest useful improvements for this single-property site, emphasizing direct and transparent routing to verified contacts, low friction, accessible alternatives, and clear expectations rather than recreating a marketplace lead funnel.

Constraints: Use public pages and primary sources. No real inquiries, calls, messages, tour bookings, account creation, or personal-data submissions during research. Do not invent contact details or imply availability/confirmed scheduling without evidence. No implementation in this task; capture proposed follow-up work and decisions needing owner input.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Comparison covers Realtor.com, Redfin, Zillow, and at least two additional major sites, with dated primary-source URLs and observed flow evidence; blocked or inferred steps are labeled.
2. Current local inquiry/contact/showing flow is mapped with source-file references and verified destination/recipient details where available.
3. Concise gap analysis distinguishes useful single-property patterns from marketplace-specific monetization or routing.
4. Prioritized recommendation maps visitor intent to CTA, destination/recipient, data/consent needs, confirmation expectations, and fallback channel, including unresolved ownership or scheduling questions.
5. Findings and implementation-ready follow-up scope are recorded in a tracked research artifact or this Bead, without modifying the site or disturbing another session's work.
notes:
Research checkpoint — 2026-10-07. Partial coverage; no code/site edits, no real inquiries, calls, emails, accounts, or bookings. Concurrent work left untouched. Repository HEAD inspected: 8c12353ade0123d311a7adc7712b334774615437. Research report below is advisory, not implementation approval.

KEY FINDING
The site's current direct brokerage/email routing is worth preserving. Major listing CTAs often acquire a buyer-agent relationship rather than contact the listing agent. On THIS Zillow Showcase listing, Contact Liz and Request a tour have explicitly different recipients. Do not generalize all Zillow buttons as paid-lead routing.

VERIFIED SOURCES AND OBSERVATIONS (all accessed 2026-10-07)
1. Zillow live 323 Colonial listing: https://www.zillow.com/homedetails/323-Colonial-Dr-Berkeley-Springs-WV-25411/22875195_zpid
- Contact Liz opens Contact Listing Agent, names Liz McDonald, displays a phone, Name/Phone/Email/Message fields and property-prefilled message. No login gate before this form. Required-field enforcement not tested; fields left blank.
- Consent says identified professional may call/text, including automated means/pre-recorded/artificial voices; consent not condition of purchase; Zillow may share recent/future site activity with agent. No submission, so actual delivery/confirmation unverified.
- Separate Request a tour explicitly says connecting with a local buyer's agent who advertises on Zillow. Select up to three preferred times, then Next. No personal information or request sent. Do not imply those times are confirmed availability.
- Listing displays open house Saturday October 10, 1–3 PM. Observation only; confirm with brokerage before publishing locally.
- Zillow Premier Agent official page fetched HTTP 200: https://www.zillow.com/pro/premier-agent/ describes Contact agent/Request a Tour -> contact info -> verification -> partner-agent connection. Generic product model does not override property-specific Contact Liz evidence.
2. Realtor.com official https://www.realtor.com/schedule-tour/ fetched HTTP 200 and read by parent. Says choose day/time window, submit request, connect with a local buyer's agent who arranges tour, then tour with matched agent. This is documented marketed flow, not observed submission. Live 323 Colonial detail page returned visible 'This is taking longer than usual'; exact live fields, consent, sign-in gates and actual recipient not verified. No retries after bounded access attempt.
3. Redfin live https://www.redfin.com/WV/Berkeley-Springs/323-Colonial-Dr-25411/home/21971085
- Distinct Request showing, Start an offer, Ask a question, and phone entry points. Showing opens preferred date/time and In person/Video tour. Next opens Join or sign in to tour (email/Google/Apple, Terms/Privacy). Stopped at this gate. Did not test offer/question submission.
- Official https://support.redfin.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001432232-Scheduling-a-Tour fetched HTTP 200 and read by parent: Redfin local team coordinates with listing agent; even an available Redfin agent slot still needs listing confirmation. Request acknowledgment is separate from email confirming home availability and assigned agent. First-tour questionnaire includes existing agent relationship, then identity verification. Do not copy this onboarding into a seller's static site.
- Same official help documents mobile-app bottom Schedule Tour -> preferred date/time -> tour mode -> overview/notes -> submit -> local-team availability confirmation. App behavior documented only, not executed.

- Tour modal: date, Morning/Afternoon/Evening; Name/Email/Message visibly required, Phone not starred, optional also-selling checkbox. Message prefilled with property. No sign-in gate before form. Submission consent includes marketing calls/texts/emails by RE/MAX LLC and/or local franchised office, automated/artificial/prerecorded contacts; consent not condition of purchase, unsubscribe language. Not submitted; actual recipient and follow-up timing unknown.

- PRODUCT.md:45–49 records owner choice of general brokerage number, not private direct mobile; preserve it. Do not replace with Zillow or Redfin contact numbers or private MLS portal URL.

RECOMMENDED MINIMUM FOLLOW-UP (NOT IMPLEMENTED)
Keep native disclosure and direct links, no backend/calendar/account/CRM yet. Preserve approved visual layout, exact listing prose and public contact choices.
A. Broaden disclosure label to cover questions and visits, e.g. Questions & showings (owner copy approval). Inside clearly name Liz as listing agent, Dandridge as brokerage, not buyer representation.
B. Two intent-specific email links to the SAME verified Liz address: Ask about this home and Request a showing by email. Prefill subject with 323 Colonial Dr, Berkeley Springs and MLS WVMO2008198; showing draft may prompt for preferred dates/times and whether buyer already has an agent. No sensitive financial/preapproval data. Use encoded native mailto; visitor reviews/sends in email app. Must explicitly say opens email app, not request sent. Display selectable email address as fallback; retain existing brokerage phone prominently.
C. For represented buyers: concise guidance that their agent can contact listing brokerage to arrange showing. Optional prompt, not forced qualification gate. Brokerage must confirm any agent-only scheduling channel before linking it.
D. State timing truth: preferred times are requests; showing arranged/confirmed by brokerage. No instant booking, text-capability or response-speed promise without approval. If brokerage has existing public property-specific showing-request system, inspect recipient/consent/confirmation and reuse it rather than build ours.
E. Keep Zillow as secondary 'View listing on Zillow' research link, not primary schedule destination. Our direct contact actions should clearly remain available before visitor leaves.
F. Optional open-house line only after owner/broker confirms Oct 10 1–3 PM, timezone, access instructions and removal/update owner. Do not auto-promote Coming Soon status.

INTENT -> CHANNEL / DATA / NEXT STEP
- Property question -> Liz email; property-prefilled subject and optional question; visitor sends through own mail client, reply from agent. Fallback visible email and office phone.
- Private showing -> Liz email or office call; preferred date windows and return contact as voluntarily supplied, agent relationship optional; appointment only after brokerage confirmation. No site-side data collection.
- Already represented -> buyer asks own agent to coordinate with listing brokerage; preserve current phone/email. Do not redirect to competing buyer-agent signup.
- Ready to offer -> own agent / listing brokerage for process, not website offer intake. No legal/financial documents collected.
- Public listing research -> explicitly labeled Zillow outbound link; platform consent/routing belongs to Zillow, separate from direct contact.

LATER ONLY IF NEEDED
A short form could help visitors without configured email apps, but first agree recipient/backup, response ownership, retention, spam protection, delivery-failure handling, brokerage-approved notice and consent. Name + one reply channel + question or preferred time should suffice initially. Distinguish backend acceptance, inbox delivery, human reply, and confirmed appointment. Never report mailto click or outbound_click as conversion. Keep existing category-only analytics; only add intent enum/event if actual decisions need it, never message bodies/contact data. Avoid custom availability calendar without authoritative brokerage scheduling integration.

OPEN DECISIONS / VERIFICATION
Confirm brokerage preferred public showing route, whether email is actively monitored with backup, represented-buyer instructions, permission for future public scheduler, and any open-house publication. No human decision needed to report these findings; no durable approval requested. Remaining research: Homes.com actual public buyer form/routing; Realtor.com live fields/consent; external-site mobile web comparisons. title: Pilot photorealistic great-room reconstruction from 360 tour and listing photos
description:
## Objective
Try a photorealistic, fixed-viewpoint 360-degree reconstruction of the great room at 323 Colonial Dr. Test whether existing references can support a faithful, attractive virtual-tour panorama before expanding to other rooms. This ticket records the experiment; creating it does not start implementation or authorize publication.

## Agreed approach
Use Zillow's existing 360-degree tour and floor plans to recover spatial relationships and approximate dimensions. Use higher-quality listing photos for materials, trim, furniture, and fine detail. Use exterior photographs to constrain roof pitch, window elevations, and ridge height. Rebuild lighting rather than baking photographed glare/shadows into materials. Build consistent geometry, not an AI-invented panorama whose architecture changes between views.

## Sources
- Zillow tour: https://www.zillow.com/homedetails/323-Colonial-Dr-Berkeley-Springs-WV-25411/22875195_zpid/?imxlb=t%2C12
- Browser inspection confirmed this is an existing Zillow 3D Home tour, with foyer, multiple living-room capture points, kitchen/dining connections, and floor-plan viewpoint markers. Inspected foyer, living-room panorama in multiple directions, and a second living-room point.
- assets/listing/manifest.json maps 73 gallery images to captions and source provenance. Not all 73 are house-interior references; some are grounds or concepts.
- Useful local images: assets/listing/02.webp (great room), 12.webp (loft overlooking room), 13.webp (hearth), 14.webp (dining), 34.webp (entry staircase), 35.webp (kitchen reverse view), 42.webp, 44.webp, 45.webp, 46.webp, 47.webp (complementary living/kitchen views), 57.webp, 58.webp, 59.webp, 61.webp (upper-level relationships). Exterior references include 01.webp, 39.webp, 40.webp, 41.webp, 69.webp, 72.webp. Recheck each image before modeling.
- images/plan-main-marketing.png and images/plan-second-marketing.png show connections, stairs, openings, and open-to-below area. They are reference drawings, not verified construction plans; reconcile discrepancies with actual photos/tour.
- PRODUCT.md, tests/fixtures/photo-coverage.json, and tests/fixtures/redfin-refresh.json describe provenance and cleaner original-photo locations. Use best available sources, not enlarged low-quality derivatives. Existing finish simulations and conceptual basement plans are not evidence of actual architecture.

## Scale and observed dimensions
Zillow floor-plan labels: Living Room 23 ft 7 in x 15 ft 11 in; Dining Room 12 ft 3 in x 9 ft 11 in; Kitchen 11 ft 6 in x 9 ft 11 in. These are separately labeled adjoining zones, not dimensions to blindly add into a single rectangle. Zillow expressly describes plans/tours as approximate and not for design purposes.
User confirms doors are standard height. Provisional modeling reference: standard hinged door slab height 80 in / 6 ft 8 in / 2.032 m, excluding frame and trim. Exact 80-inch measurement was not independently supplied or verified. Do not apply this to sliding glass doors. Use perspective-aware calibration across views, not raw pixel-height ratios from oblique photos.

## Observed great-room features
- Double-height vaulted space; sloping ceiling planes, high dormer recess/window, suspended ceiling fan, and chandelier over dining area.
- Stone surround, raised hearth, black wood-burning stove and wood mantel; deck sliders flank hearth, with tall angular glazing above.
- Entry beside stair foot; paired rectangular front windows with shelf above; upper dormer opening.
- Wood staircase with turned balusters, curved bottom handrail and decorative stair-side trim; upper loft railing overlooks room.
- Open kitchen/dining connection; granite-topped island with rounded end and metal footrail; lower ceiling beneath loft.
- Varied wood-plank flooring, light walls, visible wood-grain trim with corner rosettes, irregular stone, dark glazing grids.
- Light sectional, wood coffee table, entry bench, dining furniture, console and smaller decor. Match important silhouettes/placement first, not every prop.

## Reconstruction uncertainties
Still infer/cross-check floor-to-loft height, ceiling peak, roof pitch, wall/roof thickness, exact openings, stair dimensions and hidden surfaces. Exterior roof ridge is not finished interior ceiling height. Rectify perspective or camera-match before deriving angles. Compare interior/exterior views of matching windows. Stair riser count only gives height when riser height is known. Record assumptions and confidence; do not invent measurement precision. Stitching artifacts, clipped highlights, white balance and cast shadows limit panorama texture/color evidence.

## Smallest experiment
1. Inventory relevant references and establish a small dimension/assumption table, separating observed, user-confirmed, and inferred values.
2. Build scaled room shell, openings, stairs and visible loft/kitchen portions. Choose one existing tour capture point as camera anchor. No whole-house build.
3. Produce a plain geometry render and compare multiple views for room proportions, window alignment, ceiling slopes and stair/loft connections. Correct geometry before furnishings.
4. Add representative photo-informed materials, key trim/furniture and controlled daylight. Avoid baking photographed lighting into textures. Keep surface colors provisional where photos disagree.
5. Render one full equirectangular 360-degree panorama at chosen point, with ordinary perspective crops for comparison. Inspect full sphere including seam, ceiling and floor. Use a minimal local panorama viewer only if needed for inspection; no site redesign or deployment.
6. Record fidelity, remaining gaps, effort and a go/no-go recommendation for more viewpoints. If photorealism is not achieved, report that and identify whether better capture, measurements or modeling are limiting.

## Boundaries
No FPS controller, collision system, working doors, free movement, whole-house reconstruction, invented finished basement, or public website changes in this pilot. Interactive game behaviors are separate work. No promise of automatic photo-to-model conversion or photorealistic success. Engine/modeling tool not selected; use available tools and avoid speculative infrastructure. Verify source-use rights before republishing imagery; remote asset downloads require explicit approval and approved browser download surface. Current inspection extracted observations, not original panorama files or a 3D model.

title: Create registered annual sequences for seasonal hero/narrative
description:
## Objective
Use Nano Banana (nanobanana) and appropriate image-processing/registration tooling to create a private annual image sequence for the hero and scrolling narrative evaluated in colonial-wtm. Approximately 24 gradual frames per changing photo are in scope, with count adjustable after visual review; four seasonal targets are approval anchors, not the final deliverable. Obtain owner review of anchors before filling intermediate frames. Target continuous slow dissolves without intentional holds; final annual duration is proposed by colonial-wtm. Inventory all 73 catalog IDs, but generate only hero/narrative needs, with explicit gallery-only/invariant/non-photo exceptions. This task owns assets, exports and asset-level transition QA; colonial-wtm owns architecture and the shared contract, not implementation. Neither investigation needs to wait for the other to finish.

## Owner requirements
- Lock each photo frame: camera position, perspective, framing, crop and fixed scene geometry must not move as seasons transition.
- Rebalance interior illumination to neutral-soft white around 3500K. Bathrooms are the exception: daylight-balanced illumination. Apply these room-based targets consistently across seasons; do not substitute an overall warm filter.
- Maintain consistent styling, lighting, seasonal features and art direction across all photos.
- Inspect details, especially every view through windows: outdoor scenery visible from interiors must match the selected season and its time/lighting conditions.

## Inputs and continuity
Read colonial-29s, superseded colonial-m08 and completed colonial-1x4 before work. Use the best verified current source for each stable photo ID, preserving the 73-ID catalog and its captions/mappings. Inspect existing seasonal work and provenance; reuse approved material where suitable rather than regenerate blindly. Prior hero direction supplies a starting reference: lush dewy spring with morning golden exterior light; late summer; red fall foliage, moss/leaf litter, wispy evening sky and subtle window glow; snowy winter dusk with glowing windows. Reconcile that exterior direction with the new interior lighting requirements, including how room-appropriate interior light appears from outside. The prior unchanged late-summer hero does not exempt interior masters from requested light rebalance.

## Production approach
1. Inventory the complete set and current hero/narrative membership, classify exterior/interior/bathroom and special non-photo assets, and identify repeated views of the same rooms, building faces and landscaping. Select one fixed master per photo. Seasonal effects may be unchanged where no seasonal cue exists; shared variants are acceptable only when explicit and visually appropriate. Preserve factual plan/non-photographic assets rather than invent seasonal edits; record treatment for every catalog ID, no silent omissions. Generate no variants solely for original-photo galleries. Current contextual-link-only IDs include 15, 19, 20, 24, 31 and 32; verify source membership before production rather than assuming this list cannot change. Original gallery assets never receive the requested interior lighting rebalance; that applies only to generated hero/narrative variants.
2. Establish a compact shared visual reference and processing recipe for all four seasons: exterior time of day, sun/shadow direction, vegetation/snow/weather, room materials and furnishings, and interior light targets. Daylight-balanced bathrooms need one documented consistent target/reference; distinguish mixed exterior light through windows from interior fixture illumination. Approximately 3500K is an art-direction target, not a claim of physically measured color temperature from rendered pixels. Preserve material color and avoid clipped whites or pervasive orange/blue casts.
3. Use reference-guided Nano Banana edits from fixed masters and shared approved references. Use existing nanobanana CLI when GEMINI_API_KEY is available; never expose credentials. Do not chain independent generative edits until structure drifts. If access, budget or approval is unavailable, record the blocker rather than install tools, buy credits or switch paid providers without authority. Gate bulk anchor production on owner acceptance of four-season representative samples: exterior/hero, ordinary interior with visible outdoors, and an in-scope bathroom, plus any especially difficult view. Propose and document bathroom daylight reference and registration tolerance with those samples. After producing anchors for the scoped photo set, obtain owner review of those anchors/contact sheets before filling intermediate frames. Do not treat lack of feedback as approval.
4. Use suitable existing tooling for fixed-landmark registration, consistent crop/dimensions, masks/compositing, color comparison and exports. Anchor immovable architecture, window frames, trim, counters, fixtures and furniture. Do not align on leaves, snow or clouds. Registration alone cannot repair warped geometry: regenerate or composite when required; avoid extreme warp/stretch, invented edges or lost field of view. Preserve source resolution/detail without claiming synthetic upscaling recovers real detail.
5. Check all seasonal cues, including exterior scenes through every window and glazed door, skylights, mirrors/reflections showing outdoors, neighboring structures, snow/foliage coverage, shadows and exterior lighting. Match shared rooms/scenes across viewpoints; do not create contradictory weather, vegetation, finishes or furnishings. Seasonal changes must not invent property features, hide defects or misrepresent permanent condition.

## Quality gates
Inspect every delivered photo/frame at full resolution and in intended display sizes. Use fixed-landmark overlays/difference views and a runnable local crossfade preview, including every adjacent-frame transition, midpoint fades, repeated cycling and last-to-first annual wrap, to detect translation, zoom, rotation, perspective drift, doubled edges, crop jumps, exposure flicker and generative detail errors. Document a concrete registration tolerance and measurement method appropriate to output size before full production; supplement numerical checks with visual inspection. Transition QA must verify locked structure, not just attractive stills. Check room lighting and seasonal window consistency on every applicable image, not samples alone. Use contact sheets organized by annual phase/season, room/view and photo ID to verify whole-set coherence. Record failures and repair or explicitly hold them; do not label unchecked variants approved.

## Deliverables and boundaries
Deliver a private, reviewable approximately 24-frame annual asset set with approved seasonal anchors and stable photo-ID/annual-phase/frame mapping, originals preserved, consistent output dimensions/crops, provenance (source hashes, model/tool versions, prompts/settings and registration/color processing), contact sheets, per-photo QA status and local transition preview/check instructions. Conform to the shared contract owned by colonial-wtm: stable IDs, original fallback reference, animated/invariant/gallery-only/non-photo treatment, common phase/frame order and anchor positions, paths/naming, dimensions/crop/aspect ratio, responsive sizes/formats, byte sizes and approval/QA eligibility. Supply representative metadata and obtain contract agreement before full intermediate production/final export; never invent an incompatible producer-only format. Frame-count changes preserve a common annual phase; explicitly mapped invariant frames may reuse assets rather than duplicate files. Do not implement the global runtime. Keep working masters separate from efficient website-ready derivatives; reuse existing encoding tooling and document byte totals.
Creation of this Bead does not execute generation or authorize billing changes, new paid subscriptions, dependency installation, downloads requiring separate approval, public asset replacement, publish-allowlist changes, push or deployment. Keep generated assets and previews private/local until owner review; final marketing suitability and publication require explicit acceptance. Do not modify live listing copy, original source photos, analytics or unrelated seasonal work.
## Owner-approved scope and handoff clarification
- Only hero and scrolling narrative receive seasonal variants. Both gallery forms, enlarged viewer regardless of entry point, previous/next previews and full-size/direct links remain current approved, unchanged catalog photography. Clicking an animated photo opens its original. Keep generated/light-rebalanced variants separate; preserve source and current gallery derivative hashes, stable IDs, watermarks, captions and mappings.
- Four season anchors lead into approximately 24 gradual annual frames, not an out-of-scope future project. Frame count can change when needed for visual quality, with change recorded and coordinated with colonial-wtm. Intermediate foliage, snow, sky, window scenes and lighting must progress coherently between reviewed anchors, including winter-to-spring and final-to-first wrap. Use fixed masters/references or structure-preserving processing, not serial generative edits that accumulate drift. No requirement to fabricate variation in seasonally invariant scenes.
- Gallery-only assets and factual plans get explicit unchanged treatment across the phase mapping. The full 73-ID inventory does not authorize 73 annual sequences. Exterior/ordinary-interior/bathroom classification and room-specific lighting requirements remain mandatory for generated variants.
- colonial-wtm proposes timing and measurable runtime budgets for the actual ~24-frame scope. This ticket reports frame/export counts, byte totals and measured asset registration results; keep working masters and private provenance separate from possible future delivery derivatives. Sample review resolves numeric registration tolerance and bathroom daylight reference before scaling. If output cannot meet geometry/quality or agreed delivery budgets, hold failed assets and record the issue; do not silently lower standards, reduce count or declare completion.
- Local asset preview is for still/transition QA, including all adjacent blends and annual wrap, not a production website prototype. Later integration must additionally verify actual scroll-plus-season composition and end-to-end performance. Runtime synchronization/readiness failure policy belongs to colonial-wtm: visible images pause together rather than drift; offscreen/original-gallery assets do not block them. Default no-JS/print/reduced-motion presentation is originals.
- Both investigations may begin independently; no whole-ticket blocking dependency or circular dependency. Sample/anchor approvals and shared-contract agreement are stage gates. Accepted assets plus accepted architecture are inputs to a separately approved implementation follow-up specified by colonial-wtm. Neither current ticket owns production integration or publication.
- All work stays private/local. Public disclosure/presentation remains deferred; providing originals in galleries is not permission to publish generated imagery without later review. Existing listing copy, PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md and public files are not changed by this scope interview. Existing colonial-29s mock revisions remain separately owned; inspect/reuse only verified accepted outputs without editing that task's active files. This interview updates tickets only and does not start generation or implementation.

title: Evaluate synchronized seasonal hero/narrative architecture
description:
## Objective and owner-approved scope
Evaluate synchronized seasonal animation for the hero and scrolling narrative only, coordinated with asset production in colonial-66v. Target approximately 24 gradual annual frames per changing photo, not just four seasonal stills; frame count may change with visual need after review. Establish seasonal anchors first, obtain owner review, then fill intermediate frames. Continuous slow dissolves with no intentional holds; propose and justify full-year duration during evaluation. Neither the older 6-second hold/3-second fade nor the private mock's observed 5-second year is an approved final timing.

All new work remains private. Both gallery forms (in-page catalog and gallery.html), enlarged viewer regardless of entry point, previous/next previews, and full-size/direct image links show unchanged current catalog originals, never generated seasonal or interior-light-rebalanced derivatives. Clicking an animated hero/narrative photo opens its original. Preserve 73 stable IDs, captions, alt text, factual plan disclosure, layout and analytics semantics. Original means current approved catalog photography/derivatives, not obsolete low-quality sources.

## Inputs and implementation boundaries
Read colonial-29s, colonial-66v and current PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md; inspect private seasonal work without modifying another task's files. Query graphify-out/graph.json first if present, then verify source. Relevant seams: index.html, gallery.html, listing.js, gallery.js, listing.css, assets/listing/manifest.json and scripts/publish-files.txt. listing.js already crossfades photo identities by native scroll; gallery.js owns original-photo viewer, adjacent previews and full-size links. Reuse static-site/progressive enhancement and native browser/CSS mechanisms; no backend or new dependency without demonstrated need.

## Shared contract ownership
This ticket owns the recorded minimal asset/runtime contract; colonial-66v supplies sample metadata and produces conforming assets. Define stable photo ID, original fallback reference, animated/invariant/gallery-only/non-photo treatment, common annual phase and frame order (including four named anchor positions), frame count/phase offsets, naming/paths, per-output dimensions/crop/aspect ratio, responsive widths/formats, byte sizes and approval/QA eligibility. Keep provenance/private working metadata outside any future public delivery manifest. Invariants may reuse one file; deduplicate rather than require 24 duplicate binaries. Frame-count changes must preserve common phase semantics across photos; avoid per-photo timing drift. Contract must be agreed before intermediate full-set production/final export so producers do not guess incompatible layouts. Evaluation can use assumed suitable assets and representative metadata; it must not wait for completion of asset production.

## Runtime decisions to evaluate
- One shared annual phase for hero and narrative, not per-image clocks. Define chronological season order, initial phase, continuous dissolve curve/duration, accessible pause/resume and manual season selection. Manual selection maps to reviewed anchors. Document mid-fade pause behavior accurately, not a misleading single-season label.
- Compose seasonal blending inside existing scroll-linked photo-identity blending; do not replace native scroll progression, alter final-photo viewing steps, or introduce double-opacity darkening, blank gaps, geometry shifts or focus regressions. Verify simultaneous scroll and seasonal transitions, both directions, and quantify worst-case layer cost.
- Prefer coherence over progress: when a required visible seasonal frame is unavailable, hold all participating visible images at last coherent phase, use bounded recovery, then remain paused if failure persists. No independent seasonal drift. Decide readiness before advancing and handle mid-fade/newly visible cases explicitly. Offscreen/hidden narrative photos and original-only galleries must not block the readiness barrier. Define safe entry when scrolling exposes an unready photo: no wrong-season flash, blank frame or indefinite page-wide wait. Specify original/static fallback if no coherent initial seasonal frame exists. Original galleries remain usable during failures.
- Bound preloading, lazy loading, decoded frames, cache reuse, responsive selection, transfer and mobile GPU/memory costs for approximately 24 frames at actual narrative scale. Inventory all 73 IDs but charge generation/delivery only to animated needs. Do not eagerly load the entire annual catalog. Account for both photo-identity layers during scroll transitions and responsive-source changes.
- Define hidden-tab suspension/resume, offscreen re-entry, opening/closing nested original galleries/viewer, direct gallery navigation, history/back-forward restoration and return to narrative. Original galleries never join seasonal phase or allocate seasonal buffers. Decide whether modal visibility pauses the narrative clock and whether lightweight same-tab state is useful. No cross-tab or cross-visitor synchronization; cross-navigation phase persistence is optional, not assumed.
- Default no-JS, print and prefers-reduced-motion to unchanged original stills. Retain accessible pause/manual controls where enhancement applies, keyboard/focus behavior and original links; define live reduced-motion changes without surprise restart. Seasonal autoplay is a scoped future exception to the existing product brief's no-autoplay rule, not permission to autoplay photo identities.
- Preserve listing prose, captions, source photos and analytics/privacy boundaries. No new seasonal analytics events by default. Identify later documentation, private/public manifest separation, publish-allowlist and static hosting/build implications. Public presentation/disclosure remains deferred pending separate owner review; original-gallery access is agreed but not publication approval.

## Deliverable, verification and staged handoff
Record concise recommendation, meaningful alternatives, exact touchpoints, shared contract example covering animated/invariant/gallery-only assets, runtime lifecycle and unresolved choices with recommendations. Include quantitative transfer/decoded-memory/render-layer budgets and test device/network assumptions at ~24-frame scale; propose measurable thresholds, timing and frame-count review before implementation/full production.
Specify runnable verification strategy: shared phase including annual wrap; every adjacent-frame dissolve; simultaneous scroll/season fades; rapid scrolling/newly visible image readiness; image/decode/network failure and bounded pause/recovery; hidden-tab and modal resume; manual selection and pause mid-fade; no-JS/print/reduced-motion originals; both galleries/viewers/previews/direct links retaining original bytes and IDs; navigation/back-forward; mobile bandwidth/memory/layout and existing analytics/focus regressions. Account for screenshot tooling that can reset infinite animations; prove real phase rather than trusting a reset capture.
Document a separately approved implementation follow-up (scope and gates, not executed here): consume accepted architecture/contract and accepted assets from colonial-66v; build private hero/narrative integration, run end-to-end compositing/registration/performance QA, obtain owner acceptance, then consider publication separately. This closes the ownership gap: colonial-66v owns asset QA/local asset preview; this evaluation specifies runtime/end-to-end QA for that follow-up. Do not claim either current ticket delivers integrated website behavior.

## Coordination and authority
colonial-66v and this ticket are related, not whole-ticket blockers. Both investigations may start independently; contract agreement gates intermediate production/export, owner-approved representative anchors gate bulk anchor work, and owner approval of seasonal anchors gates intermediate filling. Accepted assets and architecture gate later integration. Do not create circular dependencies or make architecture completion depend on final imagery.
Evaluation only: no runtime implementation/prototype, photo generation/editing, public asset replacement, account/dependency changes, publish-allowlist edits, push or deployment. Existing colonial-29s mock work stays separate. This interview authorized ticket clarification only.

It designs an adjustable approximately 24-frame annual timeline with reviewed four-season anchors and continuous slow dissolves/no holds, proposes final timing, and specifies shared phase, scroll-fade composition, visible-readiness pause/recovery and offscreen/modal/navigation lifecycle. Shared asset contract has explicit owner and animated/invariant/gallery-only/non-photo examples, responsive dimensions/bytes and approval/fallback semantics; no circular dependency on finished assets. Quantitative transfer/memory/render budgets and runnable verification cases cover actual ~24-frame scope, year wrap, original galleries and no-JS/print/reduced-motion fallbacks. Separately approved implementation follow-up owns private integration and end-to-end acceptance; public disclosure/publication remains deferred. No implementation or buyer-facing changes.

title: Clarify and fix photo-position indicators for scrolling versus sequential gallery browsing
description:
## User concern
Navigation dots make sense while scrolling the page, but not while moving sequentially through every photo after choosing View all photos. Work through the intended behavior, then implement the smallest coherent fix. Preserve useful scroll-position cues rather than removing dots globally.

## Investigation and implementation
Trace homepage scroll/slideshow cues, the All 73 photos catalog, and the single-photo viewer reached from both index.html and gallery.html. Decide separately which position cue each context needs; do not assume decorative dots are interactive navigation. Evaluate removing the dense dot strip from sequential viewing and using the existing Photo N of 73 text instead. Record the chosen behavior and rationale before implementation; exact replacement remains a design decision, not an approved requirement. Check whether catalog thumbnail dots provide useful information or unnecessary clutter.

## Source context
gallery.js creates aria-hidden .photo-dots for both viewer and catalog. showPhoto updates viewer dots and #viewer-title; listing.css currently visually hides #viewer-title and catalog .photo-number. Existing tests/gallery-viewer.html asserts dot rendering and hidden viewer title, so update tests to the chosen behavior rather than preserving obsolete assertions. Preserve homepage scroll cues covered by tests/narrative-scroll.html.

## Coordination
Related active work: colonial-c50 investigates performance of the same View all photos interaction. At ticket creation gallery.js and tests/gallery-viewer.html contain uncommitted changes; coordinate before editing and preserve that work. Avoid reintroducing unnecessary dot DOM or layout work.

Remove decorative 73-dot strips from sequential viewer; expose existing Photo N of 73 heading with its polite live region. Remove repeated catalog thumbnail dots: static grid has no single current photo, and 73 tiny marks per thumbnail do not communicate useful scroll position. Keep captions, accessible photo labels/hidden catalog numbering, native scrollbar and all existing controls. Direct gallery grid remains visually unchanged. Smallest boundary: delete viewer/catalog dot creation, geometry and listeners from gallery.js; keep shared createPhotoDots/photoInset helpers used by listing.js; unhide only viewer-title in listing.css and remove obsolete gallery-only dot styles. No HTML, photo, order, analytics, dependency, persistence, or deployment change. title: Implement PostHog visit, engagement and outbound-click tracking
description:
## Objective and dependency
Implement the minimum PostHog tracking required by parent colonial-zoc, after guided setup colonial-zoc.1 supplies verified free project configuration and owner-approved privacy, geography, identity lifetime and retention decisions. Do not replace these decisions with defaults. Ticket creation is not implementation or deployment approval.

## Scope and boundaries
Read PRODUCT.md, index.html, gallery.html, gallery.js, listing.js, package.json, scripts/publish-files.txt and existing tests before editing. Reuse shared native progressive-enhancement flows and stable photo IDs from assets/listing/manifest.json; no frontend framework or bespoke analytics backend. State persistent-data/third-party boundary and smallest implementation before edits. Use normal direct-start Bead ownership workflow when implementation begins.
Preserve Cloudflare beacon (colonial-1tp), frozen listing copy/assets, reduced-motion behavior, keyboard/dialog focus, no-JS fallbacks and link navigation. New buyer assets must be deliberately included in publication allowlist; do not publish repository root. Privacy notice placement must respect existing route/test constraints or explicitly update them.

## Instrumentation
- Minimal PostHog SDK configuration using verified public project ingestion token and region host only. Disable unrequested products, identified person enrichment, replay, broad autocapture and advertising integrations. Owner-approved coordinate heatmaps are IN scope on listing/gallery paths; enforce paths in client because account URL restrictions warn they are not enforced. Verify heatmap batch sanitization, free three-URL limit and no arbitrary DOM text. Do not record forms or arbitrary DOM text. No private API keys in browser, repository or Beads.
- Approved expiring site-scoped browser linkage, no custom fingerprinting. Reuse SDK session/visit mechanics when adequate. Distinct browser is not person. A reload or cross-page navigation does not create a repeat visitor; distinguish later visits/later-day returns per accepted definition. Respect storage refusal/expiry and do not attempt identity recovery.
- Page/visit metrics for index.html and gallery.html, device category, sanitized source/campaign, approved coarse location. Keep original acquisition and return-visit sources distinct; direct/unknown remains explicit. Strip unrelated query strings, ad click IDs and personal identifiers; outbound reporting uses destination categories/domain or approved path rather than arbitrary full URLs.
- Track photo opens by stable ID and active-visible viewing-time estimates; property-details opens and visible detail/section engagement. Count only qualifying visible/active periods; hidden tabs, closed dialogs and idle time must not inflate attention. Define timing thresholds and event volume; no high-frequency heartbeat flood.
- Use one shared outbound handler for brokerage tel:, agent mailto:, Zillow and future external links; distinguish destinations and click placement if useful. Preserve keyboard activation and navigation. Do not intercept/submit communications; clicks are intent only. Do not classify same-site navigation as outbound.
- Privacy notice, usable opt-out, GPC respected before SDK/persistence/network, and own/development/test-traffic exclusion. Final owner policy: NO geographic gate, no country-based exclusion (including unknown location), and no opt-in UI. Do not add a Worker, geolocation eligibility request or fingerprinting workaround. This policy decision is not universal legal clearance; newly established applicability conflicts block live collection for owner resolution. Verify no prohibited analytics storage/read/send before eligibility is established. Blocked SDK or storage must not break website.
- GeoIP and property filters per setup: keep coarse fields only in analytics records, remove raw IP/coordinates/unneeded fields; do not claim network provider never sees IP. Retention and deletion policy match accepted compromise.

## Dashboard and verification
Configure concise owner dashboard, within confirmed free features: source/location/device groups, distinct browsers, returning browsers/visits across selected weeks, photo/detail interest, observed paths/drop-off, and outbound clicks plus distinct browser clickers. Include direct-to-contact flow. Never infer confirmed inquiry, completed Zillow conversion or exact human counts. Small location groups are approximate, potentially identifying and not proof of anonymity.
Leave a small runnable regression check using existing test tooling. Cover duplicate listener/reload behavior, browser persistence/expiry and simulated multi-day returns, opt-out and blocked storage/SDK, source sanitization, event payload minimization, active-visible timing and tel/mail/external link categorization. Run npm test and relevant existing Python/browser regression checks from PRODUCT.md. Account/live checks only with owner-authorized synthetic traffic, isolated/excluded from production reporting; verify actual ingested payload filtering, group reports and free-plan usage.
Local code completion does not prove deployed tracking. Push/deployment requires applicable explicit approval; record exact verified environment and remaining live steps rather than silently publishing. Record event schema, testing, retention and deletion responsibilities in durable handoff.

title: Guide owner through free PostHog account and privacy setup
description:
## Objective
Walk owner through creating a free PostHog Cloud account and project for 323 Colonial, then prepare an implementation-ready handoff. Parent colonial-zoc is the requirements source; read it before work. Interactive guidance is wanted, not unattended signup now.

## Work
1. Reverify current PostHog free plan, no-card/no-trial path, analytics event allowance, one-year retention, free user-path limitations, and whether required ingestion privacy transformations and reports fit free tier. No paid upgrades or billing details without new approval. Do not promise indefinite until-sale retention.
2. Explain US/EU project-region choice and create account/project with owner in control of email, credentials, terms and any MFA. Use approved trusted credential flow if operating browser; never print passwords/personal API keys or persist them in tickets. Record project identity and region, API host and safe configuration handoff; only public ingestion token may ultimately be client-side.
3. Verify supported configuration for persistent first-party pseudonymous browser IDs across weeks without creating named/person-profile enrichment. Decide expiry with owner (90 days is proposed only), define repeat visit versus reload/new tab, and clarify approximate DC city/region versus metro reporting.
4. Agree privacy policy and opt-out approach consistent with applicable law and owner preference for no opt-in where lawful. Resolve overseas/unknown-geography handling before persistent collection. Site scope is WV homeowner, US marketing; this is not a worldwide consent exemption. If material legal uncertainty requires later decision, create a durable blocker rather than assuming approval.
5. Configure or document plan to disable replay, general autocapture, identity enrichment, ad integrations and unnecessary products. Owner subsequently approved coordinate heatmaps; use final design for current scope. Check GeoIP enrichment then removal of raw IP, coordinates and unneeded properties from stored events; distinguish event storage from provider network/security logs. Verify settings really apply to free plan. No server/IP fingerprinting workaround to avoid consent.
6. Decide retention compromise if sale takes longer than free retention, including whether available exports are sufficient and who retains/deletes them. Obtain explicit decision rather than dropping history silently.
7. Prepare dashboard/report design: source + coarse location + device, distinct browsers, returning browsers/visits, photo/detail attention and outbound destination rates. Count distinct browsers clicking as well as click events. Initial versus current-visit attribution must remain distinct. No setup transmission of production visitor data.

## Handoff
Persist non-secret project/configuration facts, owner decisions, current plan evidence and remaining limitations in this task. Existing Cloudflare integration colonial-1tp stays in place. Implementation is a separate dependent task. Setup does not authorize publishing site code, deployment, repository push or paid resources.

## Verification
Owner confirms access to project; inspect actual plan and privacy controls rather than assuming defaults. Revalidate documented settings against current SDK version. Any sample events require explicit owner agreement and must be synthetic/isolated, not silently mixed with real traffic. Browser evidence, if used, must prove observed state without exposing credentials.
design:
SETUP HANDOFF — final owner decisions; not implementation, collection or deployment approval

Authority and evidence
This design supersedes earlier provisional design and chronological notes wherever they conflict. Scope is guided account setup and implementation-ready planning, not proof of installed or live analytics. Account evidence is owner screenshots/text; agent never authenticated into project or sent events. Owner chose cookies + heatmaps + no opt-in after reviewing guidance. Final explicit geographic answer: "Omit gate: no country-based exclusion from analytics." Previous Cloudflare gate exploration is withdrawn from implementation scope. No custom geographic service, country lookup or non-US/unknown-country exclusion. This records owner policy, NOT a legal conclusion or worldwide exemption. Overseas accessibility alone does not establish GDPR scope; purposeful persistent monitoring can matter. Notice/opt-out is not a substitute where consent is legally required. Material newly discovered applicability conflicts must stop live collection for owner resolution, not silently add opt-in or a gate.

Project and free-plan handoff
323 Colonial, project 647943; US Cloud dashboard https://us.posthog.com; documented ingestion host https://us.i.posthog.com. Public project token at Project > General; value not requested or stored. Obtain only public phc_ ingestion token for implementation; never personal phx_ keys, credentials or signed contract in repository/Beads. Owner confirms access, monthly free plan and no payment details. Billing screenshots: 1M free analytics events/month, matching 1M billing limit, zero usage; Upgrade/Start trial offered, not an active trial. Free pricing docs: one project, one-year analytics retention, limited paths, five subscriptions. No promise of indefinite history or complete free export. Analytics billing cap does not cap other products. Heatmaps free in app up to three URLs; toolbar heatmap viewing requires pay-as-you-go/card and is NOT approved. No trials, paid features, billing or new services approved.

Observed/account controls
Earlier screenshots verified frontend autocapture, web vitals, dead clicks, session replay, heatmaps and person last-seen OFF, with no-events banner. Owner subsequently selected heatmaps; current enabled toggle is NOT independently verified. Replay stays OFF; disabled console/network suboptions do not mean active recording. Display labels such as email/name are not evidence of ingestion. Owner explicitly confirms DPA SIGNED and IP discard enabled on EXISTING project 647943, not merely organization default. Agent has not inspected signed DPA or stored events. Owner was guided to disable organization AI training on anonymized data and enable default IP discard, then acknowledged completing guidance; saved AI opt-out state not independently verified. Check correct Product and Model Development opt-out before first event; terms 5.1 is prospective only. Organization IP default affects new projects only.

Heatmap account guidance owner marked "ok done": approved screenshot hostnames left blank (these govern bot-protection bypass-cookie delivery, not page capture). Capture URLs Only listed URLs: https://323colonial.github.io/ and https://323colonial.github.io/gallery.html; optional third https://323colonial.github.io/index.html if that alias receives traffic. Optional third inclusion and actual heatmap ON state remain unverified. UI warns URL rules are NOT YET ENFORCED: client path restrictions are required, not reliance on account list. Test query/campaign matching and free three-URL counting. Coordinate heatmaps approved; broad autocapture Clickmap not approved. Geographic latitude/longitude must be removed; heatmap screen x/y are necessary approved feature, not geographic coordinates.

Resolved owner policy
- Persistent first-party random browser linkage using cookies, NOT cookieless/daily IP-user-agent hash or fingerprinting. No named/person-profile enrichment, identify/alias/group/profile setters, ad integrations or arbitrary forms/DOM text.
- Browser ID expires 90 days ABSOLUTE from creation, not rolling renewal. Rotate on next eligible visit with no link to old ID; clearing/opt-out can end sooner. Rotation does not erase already-stored events. Cookie expiry alone does not enforce localStorage/absolute TTL.
- Notice + usable opt-out, no opt-in UI; honor GPC before analytics load/read/storage/send. No geographic gate or exclusion; unknown coarse location is unknown, not inferred from timezone/language.
- Coarse country, state/region and approximate city; Washington DC is city, not metro. No raw IP or geographic coordinates in stored analytics. Provider transport/security logs are separate, not promised absent.
- Rolling ONE YEAR of detailed events accepted even if sale takes longer. Owner stops collection and deletes analytics after sale. No indefinite retention/export archive commitment.
- Preserve existing Cloudflare beacon colonial-1tp; no changes to listing copy/assets, navigation, accessibility or no-JS experience.

SDK/ingestion implementation plan (colonial-zoc.2)
Select/pin current SDK; verify actual payloads/config before live use. person_profiles: never; current capture_heatmaps option (enable_heatmaps deprecated); disable replay, general autocapture, dead clicks, performance/network/vitals, errors, surveys, flags/experiments and unnecessary products. Explicit pageview/pageleave and approved engagement events as needed. Check advanced_disable_flags also disables remote configuration, so all selected capture settings must be explicit. No identify/alias/group/person setters; disable/null internal_or_test_user_hostname person-processing behavior and avoid profile-based test markers. Use disableDeviceModel to suppress high-entropy model collection and cross_subdomain_cookie false.

Use before_send allowlisting and URL/referrer sanitization, but inspect selected SDK heatmap batching: do not assume all heatmap payloads traverse same event hook. Preserve only approved screen coordinates and sanitized paths, no raw queries/referrers/DOM text. Local/development/owner/synthetic exclusion must not create profiles. Existing internal-test report filter membership is unverified and default for new insights OFF; dashboard filters alone are not ingestion suppression.

Client ip:false is deprecated and has NO EFFECT in current SDK reference. Project IP-discard is owner-confirmed, but GeoIP ordering/coarse enrichment and actual stored payload removal need verification. Hosted transformations are documented free; errors/performance can quarantine/disable them, so an unverified transformation is not sufficient sole privacy boundary. Determine fail-safe means to retain coarse geography without storing IP/precise coordinates; don't add proxy/backend or silently drop coarse-location requirement. If hosted stack cannot meet approved privacy invariant, record blocker and seek owner decision. No browser fingerprinting workaround.

Opt-out/GPC checked BEFORE loading SDK or touching analytics persistence. Opt-out stops collection and clears analytics identifiers, distinct from historical server-event deletion. Storage refusal/blocked SDK must not break site. No cached eligibility may override opt-out. Test absolute ID expiry and source reset, no identity recovery.

Reports and event definitions
Proposed visit: SDK session separated by 30 minutes inactivity; reload/new tab/cross-page navigation alone does not create new visit. Later-day returning browser uses US/Eastern project timezone; same-day subsequent sessions separate. Distinct browsers are not unique humans, and expiry/devices/storage clearing distort counts. Never present individual dossiers.

Keep first acquisition source separate from current-visit source; allow only approved channel/campaign labels, no recipient/ad-click IDs. Direct/unknown explicit. Device category and coarse-location splits. Photo opens by stable ID, active-visible time per enlarged photo; details/section opens and visible attention. Hidden/idle time excluded, no high-frequency flood. One shared outbound handler for tel/mail/Zillow/future external links; sanitized destination/category and placement, not arbitrary full URLs. Counts AND distinct clicking browsers/rates per destination; direct-to-contact valid, no completed call/email/showing inference. Basic grouped trends/paths/funnels/SQL only within free features. Private dashboard, no public links. No paid lifecycle/group assumptions.

Remaining implementation/pre-live gates (not completed by setup)
1. Obtain public ingestion token, choose/pin SDK, inspect paths and heatmap transport, implement policy and small regression checks using existing project tooling. Run npm test and relevant PRODUCT.md Python/browser checks. Local mocks/offline tests are not live ingestion evidence.
2. Confirm saved product/model-development opt-out and intended heatmap setting before first event. Verify actual IP/coordinate removal, coarse geography, no person profiles, TTL/opt-out/GPC, sanitized heatmap payloads and free-volume bounds. Synthetic account events require separate explicit permission and isolation/exclusion; none authorized or sent during setup. No production visitors as test data.
3. Configure private free reports and verify distinction between event counts and distinct browsers. No events yet means populated dashboard/report correctness remains unverified.
4. Site push/publication/deployment needs separate applicable approval. No Worker or other custom geographic backend in scope. Owner policy is settled; no remaining setup choice blocks local implementation planning. Technical verification and any concrete newly discovered legal conflict still block live collection until resolved. Ticket creation/setup closeout is not implementation or deployment permission.

Primary references (verified during setup; recheck selected SDK in implementation)

https://posthog.com/docs/toolbar/heatmaps
https://posthog.com/docs/references/posthog-js/types/PostHogConfig

https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/what-are-the-pecr-rules/
Detailed research and evidence history remain in notes. Browser proof not completed after owner SOCKS failure; no additional screenshots required for setup closeout. No source edits, account changes by agent, visitor events, paid resources, push or deployment during setup.

title: PostHog analytics: repeat-browser groups, sources and engagement
description:
## Objective
Extend existing Cloudflare page analytics with free hosted PostHog reporting for a single-property listing operated personally by a West Virginia homeowner, marketed to US audiences and hosted at https://323colonial.github.io/.

User's exact intent: "4-5 individuals from DC" repeat visit, came from XX, and clicked through to YY. Report aggregate groups of pseudonymous browsers, NOT named people or individual dossiers. Multiweek linkage is wanted; daily-only deduplication is insufficient. Shared devices, cleared storage, changing networks, VPNs and multiple devices limit inference. Label reports as browsers/visits and approximate geography.

## Requirements
- Source attribution: Facebook/Instagram organic, personal texts/email/neighborhood groups, Substack, search and direct/unknown. Use channel/campaign tags, never recipient identifiers. Distinguish initial acquisition source from each return visit's source; do not invent missing attribution.
- Recognize repeat browsers across weeks. Report distinct browsers, visits, browsers returning on later days, event totals and distinct browsers clicking. Present grouped source/location/device reports, not dossiers.
- Coarse IP-derived location (country/state/region; clarify DC city versus metro). Do not retain raw IP or coordinates in analytics event records when coarse location suffices; provider transport/logging practices need separate verification.
- Photo opens and active-visible viewing-time estimates per enlarged photo; property-details opens and visible detail/section attention. Report group funnels and exploration/drop-off patterns split by source and mobile/desktop. Direct-to-contact visits remain valid; browsing is not mandatory funnel behavior.
- Track existing brokerage tel:, agent mailto:, Zillow and future external links automatically, with separate destination/category reporting. Clicks are intent, NOT completed calls, emails, showings or downstream Zillow outcomes. Last observed action is NOT proof of lost interest.
- Hosted dashboard owner checks on demand. Free only, minimal upkeep; no custom backend or self-hosting by default.
- User wants detailed history until sale. Free PostHog pricing verified during research: 1M analytics events/month, one project, one-year retention, no card; free paths have limitations. Reverify current limits and resolve sale exceeding retention/free export needs before promising completion.

## Selected solution (owner decisions in colonial-zoc.1)
PostHog Cloud selected: persistent first-party random browser ID with approved 90-day ABSOLUTE lifetime; no identify/name/email enrichment, replay, broad autocapture or ad integrations. Explicit events plus owner-approved coordinate heatmaps. Final owner policy: cookies, notice + opt-out, no opt-in, NO geographic gate or country-based exclusion, including unknown location. Coarse country/state/approximate city (DC city, not metro); rolling one-year history accepted, stop collection/delete after sale. Final colonial-zoc.1 design is handoff source of truth; policy choice is not worldwide legal clearance or deployment approval.
User prefers no opt-in popup where lawful. Persistent linkage is pseudonymous even when person-profile objects are disabled. Cookie/localStorage choice is not a legal exemption. Do not silently add a banner, fingerprinting workaround, or claim worldwide legality. Resolve applicable deployment policy with owner; block live persistent collection if unresolved. Consent-free aggregate statistical exceptions do not automatically permit retaining linked individual histories. PostHog cookieless server-hash mode resets daily and omits GeoIP enrichment, so it fails this requirement.

## Current project and scope
Existing Cloudflare integration: colonial-1tp (closed); owner reported live dashboard verification. Preserve it unless owner approves replacing/removing it. Product pages: index.html and gallery.html; gallery.js and listing.js own progressive enhancements. PRODUCT.md documents frozen listing content and publication boundaries. scripts/publish-files.txt is the buyer-only publish allowlist. Preserve existing UX/accessibility/fallbacks and approved listing copy/assets.
This request creates work items only. No signup, account mutation, code changes, billing, push or deployment authorized by ticket creation. Later setup is guided with owner; deployment requires separate applicable approval.

## Primary research references (reverify during setup)
https://posthog.com/product-analytics/pricing
https://posthog.com/docs/getting-started/identify-users
https://posthog.com/docs/data/anonymous-vs-identified-events
https://posthog.com/docs/libraries/js/persistence
https://posthog.com/tutorials/property-filter
https://posthog.com/tutorials/cookieless-tracking
Vendor wording "anonymous" is not legal clearance. Account secrets, personal API keys and credentials must never enter public repository or Beads.
acceptance_criteria: Guided free-account setup and dependent tracking implementation are completed and verified. Reports show distinct browsers and repeat visits across weeks by source, coarse location and device, plus photo/detail engagement and outbound destinations. Privacy/geographic policy and retention compromise are explicitly resolved before live collection; no unsupported claims of unique people, exact location, anonymity or universal consent exemption.
